text:
rachel: heads-up — saw a weird spike in provisional billing for customer ACME during a streaming session. looks like a toolcall truncated on reconnect and the ledger recorded both partial and resumed tokens.
omar: do you have the session id or sample trace? could be the ack/handoff window again
rachel: trace attached from console, session=svc-89ab, route=gpu-pool-2. logs show client reconnect -> router handed to new worker -> toolcall TTL expired while stream resumed.
mia: hmm that sounds like the same double-credit we saw with short TTL toolcalls + partial truncation. billing-bot showed provisional then final but provisional stuck in UI for a while :/ :eyes:
ken: can you paste the snippet? curious about the sequence
rachel: sure:

```
[12:03:21] incoming stream start session=svc-89ab reqid=R123
[12:03:23] toolcall start id=T99 ttl=2s
[12:03:24] client reconnect
[12:03:24] router -> worker B, new reqid=R124
[12:03:25] toolcall ttl expired on worker A; partial tokens recorded
[12:03:27] stream resumed on worker B, appended tokens accepted
```
mia: so worker A committed a partial toolcall charge, then B resumed and generated additional tokens. no single dedupe key across reconnections.
omar: root cause: we rely on reqid for dedupe, but reconnects generate a new reqid. session id is stable but we don't propagate toolcall-id across the reconnect boundary.
tia: billing-bot: provisional_credit 42 tokens recorded at 12:03:25 for svc-89ab (worker A)
billing-bot: final_credit 65 tokens recorded at 12:03:28 for svc-89ab (worker B)
ken: UX question — should console treat provisional as authoritative until final settles? users get confused when they see a provisional spike then drop.
rachel: short-term mitigation ideas:
- change router to preserve toolcall metadata (toolcall-id) across reconnects when session id matches
- add provisional->final lineage in console (show "provisional from worker A -> adjusted by worker B")
mia: agreed. quick server patch to attach stable toolcall id to session would prevent double charge in most reconnect cases.
omar: implementation note: need to ensure we don't accidentally disable legitimate retries where toolcall should run twice. must only dedupe when server confirms toolcall start but not completed and the same toolcall-id is seen on resume.
tia: billing-bot: queued ticket #INF-3217 created for provisional reconciliation run and manual audit on ACME
rachel: long-term: consider a single canonical ledger event per session/toolcall pair with state transitions (PENDING -> COMMITTED -> RECONCILED) rather than independent token writes. helps UI and accounting.
ken: sounds good. one more ask — add a dashboard telemetry tile for "provisional-final delta" per route so SRE/CS can spot spikes early.
omar: I'll own the router-preserve patch (small change to handshake). can pair with mia for tests.
mia: i'll add unit + e2e test simulating reconnect mid-toolcall + TTL expiry, and a synthetic job to run reconciliation on historical data.
rachel: thanks. can someone post the quick rollback plan if the patch regresses? we need an easy toggle in router to opt out per-customer.
omar: will add a feature-flag and a canary rollout policy. put it behind ff:toolcall-sticky and default off for 24h.
tia: billing-bot: note added to ticket INF-3217: FF gate + canary plan + console alert for affected customers
rachel: cool. follow-ups: ken — dashboard tile; mia — tests + reconciliation job; omar — router patch + FF; i'll coordinate with CS on ACME messaging.
ken: on it. will mock a small widget in console and share tomorrow.
mia: starting tests now. will push a branch.
omar: branch created: preserve-toolcall-reqid. link: https://git.local/r/preserve-toolcall-reqid
rachel: great. thanks team :thumbsup:
